### Like Father, Like Son
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/like-father-like-son
Passage: 2 Samuel 13:1-22
Points:
- Amnon treated his half-sister Tamar as a mere object to satisfy his selfish lust.
- King David was oblivious to warning signs in his household and unwittingly facilitated Amnon's trap.
- David's previous sin with Bathsheba dulled his moral discernment, leading to passive anger rather than righteous justice.
- Tamar resisted the evil and appealed to God's law, but Amnon violated her and cast her out in hatred.
- Habitual and unrepentant sin numbs the human conscience, making daily sanctification vital to recognizing right from wrong.

### When It Comes to Abuse, It Takes a Village
Author: Glen Scrivener
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/abuse-takes-village/
Passage: 2 Samuel 13:1-22
Points:
- Amnon disguised predatory selfishness as affection, which rapidly flipped into callous contempt once he had violated Tamar.
- Jonadab functioned as a shrewd enabler who encouraged the royal prince to seize what was forbidden.
- David felt intense anger but remained entirely passive, abandoning his duty as king and father to protect the vulnerable.
- Absalom silenced Tamar with a false peace to manage the scandal quietly rather than bringing truth into the open.
- While the earthly house of David failed tragically, Christ the true King protects the broken and establishes righteousness.

### Bible Pathways 04/15/2003
Author: Bible Pathways Ministries
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/biblepathways/bible-pathways-04-or-15-or-2003-1195302.html
Passage: 2 Samuel 13:1-22
Points:
- Amnon used deception and feigned sickness to trap and overpower Tamar in direct defiance of God's law.
- After indulging his lust, Amnon immediately rejected Tamar, abandoning her to live in desolate sorrow.
- David was infuriated by Amnon's outrageous sin but failed to administer the legal consequences demanded by Scripture.
- Parents experience intense heartache when their past moral compromises and sins resurface in the lives of their children.
- Although past failures cannot be erased, believers can receive true reconciliation and forgiveness through Jesus Christ.

### What Women Today Can Learn from the Tragic Story of David’s Daughter, Tamar
Author: Eva Marie Everson
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/faith/bible-study/what-women-today-can-learn-from-the-tragic-story-of-davids-daughter-tamar.html
Passage: 2 Samuel 13:1-22
Points:
- Tamar courageously attempted to reason with Amnon, appealing to his conscience, God's law, and the public shame of sin.
- David failed to discern his son's harmful scheme and later neglected to take disciplinary action against Amnon.
- Absalom urged Tamar to keep quiet, leaving her in isolation and despair while nursing bitter, vengeful hatred.
- The unraveling of David's family illustrates the severe fallout of unaddressed and unrepented sin within a home.
- Victims of sexual violence are reminded that their identity is not defined by their trauma and that God remains close to the brokenhearted.
